full_judgment: 7. The facts of this case stand as one of the naked examples of high-handedness on the part of the concerned officials of the respondents No.1. It appears that the Ministry of Industries and Commerce, Commerce Division, Government of Bangladesh, wanted to sell some of its abandoned properties including the commercial premises at 25, Bangabandhu Avenue, Dhaka, as such, a public notice was published in the daily newspaper on 11-5-1982 (Annexure-B), inviting sealed tenders for sale of the said abandoned properties. In response, the petitioners submitted their tender on 22-6-1982 and a Section Officer (AP) of the Ministry of Commerce, by its Memo No. 7(17)-FIN/82/134 dated 9-4-1984 (Annexure-C), accepted their tender. The petitioners by their letter dated 12-4-1984 (Annexure-D) prayed for some financial adjustments which was readily accommodated by the respondent No.1 by Memo No. 7(l7)-FIN/82/ 157 dated 22-4-1984 (Annexure-E). But it appears, that one Messers Yacoob Ahmed Brothers (Pakistan) Ltd, filed a suit for declaration that the case-property is not an abandoned property and the same was not vested in the respondent No.1. The said suit although was dismissed by the judgment and decree dated 27-2-1984 but the plaintiff filed a first appeal being FA No. 6 of 1984 against the Government and the parties were directed to maintain status quo by an Order dated 5-4-1984, passed by the High Court Division, till hearing of the Rule in Civil Rule No. 178(F) of 1984 (Annexure-F). In the meantime, the petitioners by their letter dated 5-5-1984 (Annexure-G) prayed for instruction from the respondent No. 1 as to whether they should deposit the down payment in favour of the Government with formal handing over of physical possession of the case-property in their favour but the Government by its Memo. No. MCIDSP/(A)/19-5/33/83 (Shadow)1214 dated 6-6-1984 (Annexure-H) informed the petitioners, about the inability of the Government to hand over physical possession of the case-property because of the Order of the Hon'ble High Court Division directing maintenance of status quo. Thereafter, in due course, the said First Appeal was dismissed by the judgment and order dated 4-3-1991, passed by the High Court Division (Annexure-I), Immediately, on receipt of the said news, the petitioners, by their letter dated 4-7-1991 (Annexure-J), prayed for handing over of the possession of the case-property on receipt of the bid money, but the respondent No. 1 without responding to their prayer, by their Memo No. MC/(AP)/7(17)-FIN/82 dated 5-8-1991 (Annexure-K), demanded arrear rents for the portion of the premises occupied by the petitioners since the sale-price of the case-property was not recovered from them. Accordingly, the petitioners promptly paid their rentals from the period from 1-1-1981 to 30-6-1991 by their pay order dated 10-8-1991 and also renewed their prayer to the respondent No. 2 by their letter dated 11-8-1991 (Annexure-M) wanted to know under what head of account they would deposit the sale-price of the case-property but instead of replying to their query, the Deputy Commissioner. Dhaka by his Memo No. 120-AP(Ba)/92 dated 27 -5-1992(Annexure-L) again asked for the monthly rents only.
